text: Long day? Time to unwind with your favorite game. You hit 'Start', eager for action, ready to jump right in.
But then, the dreaded loading screen appears. A progress bar crawls, and time seems to stretch endlessly.
And there it is: a 'helpful' tip. 'Press X to jump'. Really? Doesn't the game already know you know that? You feel mocked.
But the system knows something deeper. Loading isn't just technical; it's psychological. Those tips aren't just for you to *read*.
They're a subtle distraction, making the wait *feel* shorter. For new players, they're gentle nudges, reinforcing basic mechanics without a formal tutorial.
Next time you see a loading screen tip, you'll know it's not just placeholder. It's a designed element, quietly shaping your experience.
